title: Find Undocumented (public)
summary: Uses query find to list indexed symbols filtered by documentation state, kind, or visibility
intro: Read this when you want to know which public symbols still lack a DocInsight comment. query find with --no-docs and --public lists them; --doc-tag and --doc-contains filter by comment content instead. Also under drag-lint > Code Quality in the IDE.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint query find [--doc-tag X | --doc-contains Y | --decl-contains Z | --no-docs] [--kind K] [--name N] [--unit U] [--public] [--db ...]
help: drag-lint query find         [--doc-tag X | --doc-contains Y | --decl-contains Z | --no-docs] [--kind K] [--name N] [--unit U] [--public] [--db ...]
^ --no-docs is a FILTER (UNDOCUMENTED symbols only), not "hide the docs" -- to list them all use query --kind <k> --all
^ --decl-contains searches the DECLARING SOURCE LINE (`stored X`, `default V`, `read F write S`)
-- clauses the index does not model. Needs --kind, --name or --unit; it re-reads source per candidate.

pitfalls: --no-docs is a FILTER (UNDOCUMENTED symbols only), not "hide the docs" -- to list them all use query --kind `<k>` --all
--decl-contains searches the DECLARING SOURCE LINE (`stored X`, `default V`, `read F write S`) -- clauses the index does not model. Needs --kind, --name or --unit; it re-reads source per candidate.
case-insensitive, over /// blocks and harvested // above a declaration.
declaration clauses the index does not model. `query --text` sees string literals and comment prose, not declaring lines -- this reads the declaring line instead.
